name: Airwallex
summary: Multi-currency business accounts, corporate cards, international transfers and payment acceptance.
best_for: companies invoicing or paying in several currencies, where a 0.5% spread against your bank's 2–3% is the whole business case
skip_if: you bill in one currency and pay domestic suppliers — the multi-currency machinery is the product, and without FX volume you are paying a platform fee for a bank account
honest_knock: The honest headline here is that the FX markup is published at all — 0.5% and 1% above interbank is a real number, and most competitors will not print one. What the page does not settle is everything around it. The Grow plan's platform fee 'varies with team size' with no table, so the $12 a user is not the whole subscription -- though their table does say the first ten Spend users are free, which is the part the headline rate hides in your favour. Chargeback and dispute fees are not priced anywhere, only mentioned as a feature. And the page's own disclaimer says per-transaction fees apply to certain transactions with the detail in a separate fee schedule. So: use the published FX rate to compare against your bank, then ask for the fee schedule and the platform fee before you move money. It also helps to know whose balance sheet holds what. The US page names Airwallex US, LLC as a licensed money transmitter (NMLS #1928093) that works with Lead Bank and Evolve Bank & Trust, both Member FDIC, for some US customers; the card is issued by Community Federal Savings Bank; and Yield is a brokerage product of Airwallex Capital US LLC that invests in AAA-rated money market funds, such as those from JP Morgan Asset Management. Support differs by plan too: the plan cards put a dedicated account manager and onboarding support on Accelerate only.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month per active Spend user plus a team-size platform fee

plans.name: Grow
plans.price: $12 per active Spend user/month plus platform fee
plans.includes: first 10 users free; $12 rate up to 250 Spend users

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (2026-08-28, read off their own pricing page and fee table; re-read 2026-10-11 on airwallex.com/en-us/pricing: plans, FX, transfer, card and billing rates unchanged; re-read 2026-10-23 on the same page: plans and rates again unchanged, with a 0.4% per-transaction fee for automatic tax calculation in the billing table that our earlier readings did not record, and restamped Yield figures) FX conversion 0.5% above the interbank rate for major currencies and 1% for all others. Local transfers to 120+ countries free; SWIFT transfers $15–$25 each. Payment acceptance 2.8% + $0.30 on domestic cards and 4.30% + $0.30 on international cards; local payment methods $0.30 plus method-specific fees. Corporate cards carry no international fees and up to 2% cash rebate on local USD spend. Account plans: Explore free, Grow $12 per active Spend user/month plus a platform fee that varies with team size, Accelerate custom. Their table adds limits the earlier reading did not record: the first 10 Spend users are free and the $12 rate runs to 250 Spend users; the monthly fee is charged per business legal entity, with up to 3 entities included; for each additional entity the footnote now says only that additional fees may apply (our 28 August reading recorded $1,000); subscription and usage-based billing cost 0.50% per successful transaction while invoicing is free; and USD balances earn a Yield rate that Airwallex restamps daily rather than fixing per plan — on 23 October 2026 the US page showed 3.44% on Explore, 3.59% on Grow and 3.71% on Accelerate (3.42%, 3.57% and 3.69% on 11 October), and its own footnote reads that the indicative rate is the 7-day annualized historical rate of the underlying funds as of October 22, 2026, net of fees. Read those three figures as a moving number carrying the date the page gave it, not as a plan feature: they were 3.21%, 3.36% and 3.48% when we first recorded them on 28 August and 3.22%, 3.37% and 3.49% on 5 and 19 September.
